extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, IP statisticians, patent office officials, researchers and analysts using WIPO patent statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological notes for interpreting and using WIPO patent and related IP statistical indicators (definitions, selection rules, data caveats and comparability limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication delay for published applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to published patent applications. There is a minimum 18-month delay between application date and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should note that figures are based on published applications only and therefore reflect at least an 18-month lag from filing; this affects interpretation of recent-year trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping IPC to technology fields
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO’s International Patent Classification (IPC) technology concordance table was used to convert IPC symbols into 35 corresponding fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an electronic version of the IPC technology concordance table, visit www.wipo.int/en/web/ip-statistics. This mapping underpins field-level breakdowns and should be consulted for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of top origins (figures/tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: The top 10 origins were selected based on their 2020–2022 total published applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading charts showing 'top origins', remember they are selected by this multi-year published-application total, not by single-year filings or grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology definitions and IPC correspondence caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence between International Patent Classification (IPC) symbols and technology fields is not always apparent (there is no one-to-one correspondence). It is therefore difficult to capture all patents within a specific technology field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPC-based definitions are likely to capture the vast majority of patent applications in a given technology area, but users should be cautious: some relevant patents may be missed and some included records may be only partially relevant. For definitions of specific technologies (e.g., fuel cell, geothermal, solar, wind, hydro) see annex A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender attribution method for inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to attribute gender to inventors’ names recorded in PCT applications, WIPO produced a world gender–name dictionary based on information from 13 different public sources. Gender is attributed to a given name on a country-by-country basis, because certain names may be considered male in one country but female in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should be aware of potential misclassification and cultural variation; the method is name-based and therefore imperfect, especially for ambiguous or non‑binary names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data reference: published PCT/patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to published PCT applications / published patent applications (varies by figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many indicators are built on published application records (including PCT publications); interpretation should consider publication practices and lags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top origins inclusion criteria for GDP-normalised indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The top 20 origins were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 25 billion PPP and more than 100 resident patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This selection rule constrains which economies appear in GDP-normalised comparisons; small economies or those with few filings are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top origins inclusion criteria for population-normalised indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The top 20 origins were included if they had a population greater than 5 million and if they had more than 100 resident patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Population‑normalised charts omit small-population economies and those with very few filings; interpret omissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: GDP data specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: GDP data are in 2021 US purchasing power parity (PPP) dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users comparing patent counts per GDP should use the same PPP base year for consistency (2021 PPP dollars here).

rubrics_metrics.name: R&D expenditure data lag
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: R&D data refer to gross domestic expenditure on research and experimental development (GERD). R&D data lag by one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When correlating patent indicators with R&D, align years appropriately because GERD figures are one year behind the patent data.

rubrics_metrics.name: World totals and office coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 140 offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global aggregates are estimates from a multi-office collection and may be impacted by missing office data or methodological differences across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and interpretation of patents-in-force percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as the number of patent applications filed in year t and in force in 2023, divided by the total number of patent applications filed in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent holders must pay maintenance fees to maintain validity; patents may lapse for commercial/technological reasons. Example summary: data for 89 offices show 36.2% of applications for which patents were granted remained in force for at least 10 years after application date, and about 17.5% lasted the full 20-year term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caveat for examination outcome shares
rubrics_metrics.description: The share of applications granted should not be interpreted as grant rates, as they are based on the examination date rather than the date when the application was filed. The number of grants in a given year relates to applications filed in previous years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of differing time lags and office procedures, do not equate 'share granted in year X' with a grant probability for applications filed in year X; exercise caution when comparing offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of pending applications categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending application data are separated between (a) all patent applications, at any stage in the process, that are awaiting a final decision by a patent office, including those for which applicants have not filed a request for examination (where applicable), and (b) patent applications undergoing examination for which the applicant has requested examination (where such a request is necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because offices differ (automatic vs request-for-examination systems), presenting both categories helps account for procedural differences when comparing pending backlogs across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency time measurement caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Average pendency times for first office action and final decision are compiled for selected offices, but WIPO collects data using a common questionnaire and methodology; differences in patent procedures between offices mean data cannot be fully harmonized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise caution when comparing pendency across offices; procedural and definitional differences (e.g., when counting 'start' and 'end' events) can affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) definition and data note
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent prosecution highway is a bilateral agreement between two offices enabling applicants to request a fast-track examination whereby patent examiners can utilize work already undertaken by the other office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH flow figures show requests by office of first filing and office of later examination. Some data use an 'office of earlier examination' basis (noted with an asterisk); users should consult footnotes for such caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model data comparability caveat (China pre-2017)
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals for utility model applications are WIPO estimates using data covering 83 patent offices. China’s pre-2017 data are not comparable owing to a change in methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the methodological break in China’s series and its large filing volume, world-level growth calculations (notably 2017) may be distorted; interpret trends with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin determination for utility model applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of UM (utility model) applications is determined by the residence of the first named applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing origin shares for utility models, use residence of the first applicant as the defining rule; this may differ from other origin definitions in other tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism deposit importance for biotechnology patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits of microorganisms for patent procedures are important for biotechnological inventions. Disclosing an invention is a requirement for receiving a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics on microorganism deposits are relevant for biotech patenting activity and reflect procedural requirements (e.g., deposit obligations to meet disclosure), so include them when analysing biotech filing patterns.
